A strong password is long, random, and used in only one place. Length matters most: each extra letter multiplies the guessing work, while a clever-looking short password falls quickly to a machine that tries millions of guesses. A strong password is drawn from a wide set of letters, numbers, and marks, and it holds no name, date, or common word that a dictionary attack could try first.

History

Passwords began with the first shared computers. In the 1960s the Compatible Time-Sharing System at MIT asked each user for a password, and the idea spread to every system after it. Early passwords were short words, and attackers learned to guess them by trying whole dictionaries, so guidance grew: longer passwords, mixed character sets, and a different password for every place. In 1988 the Morris worm guessed weak passwords across the early internet, and in 2017 the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology published guidance favouring long, memorable passwords over forced, frequent changes. Generators grew up to make strong passwords that no person has to invent or remember alone. A strong password is long, random, and used in only one place. program:
"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 1: What Makes a Password Strong.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'what makes password strong'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 1: What Makes a Password Strong")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-1", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-1", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-1", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-1-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be

import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'random means unpredictable randomness works'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)

    return length * math.log2(pool_size)

    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"

pw12 = seeded_password("record-4", 12, sets)

"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 6: The Dice Method: Rolling Words.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'dice method rolling words'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 6: The Dice Method: Rolling Words")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-6", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-6", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-6", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-6-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 9: Changing Passwords: When and Why.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'changing passwords when'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 9: Changing Passwords: When and Why")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-9", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-9", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-9", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-9-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'copy paste moving password safely'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 11: Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-11", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-11", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-11", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-11-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'symbols when marks help when they hurt'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 16: Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-16", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-16", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-16", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-16-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']

LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)

    return length * math.log2(pool_size)

    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"

"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 19: Temporary Passwords: One Use Only.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'temporary passwords only'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 19: Temporary Passwords: One Use Only")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-19", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-19", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-19", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-19-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 21: Keyboard Patterns to Avoid.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'keyboard patterns avoid'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 21: Keyboard Patterns to Avoid")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-21", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-21", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-21", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-21-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))

UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"

    pool = "".join(sets)

history: Passwords began with the first shared computers. In the 1960s the Compatible Time-Sharing System at MIT asked each user for a password, and the idea spread to every system after it. Early passwords were short words, and attackers learned to guess them by trying whole dictionaries, so guidance grew: longer passwords, mixed character sets, and a different password for every place. In 1988 the Morris worm guessed weak passwords across the early internet, and in 2017 the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology published guidance favouring long, memorable passwords over forced, frequent changes. Generators grew up to make strong passwords that no person has to invent or remember alone. program:
"""Password-generator demo for the Password Generator Service record 24: The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index.
A small working generator: a seeded, deterministic draw from the four
character sets, plus a strength meter. The live tool uses the browser's
secure random source; this demo uses a seeded hash so its output can be
checked byte for byte."""
import hashlib, math
TITLES = ['What Makes a Password Strong', 'Length First: Why Longer Beats Clever', 'Letters, Numbers, and Marks: The Four Sets', 'Random Means Unpredictable: How Randomness Works', 'Passphrases: Four Words in a Row', 'The Dice Method: Rolling Words', 'Avoiding Names, Dates, and Common Words', 'One Password Per Place: Why Reuse Fails', 'Changing Passwords: When and Why', 'Storing Passwords: Memory and Keepers', 'Copy and Paste: Moving a Password Safely', 'Reading a Strength Meter', 'The 12-Character Minimum', 'The 16-Character Standard', 'The 20-Character Vault Password', 'Symbols: When Marks Help and When They Hurt', 'Pronounceable Passwords: Easy to Say, Hard to Guess', 'PINs: Short Numbers and Their Limits', 'Temporary Passwords: One Use Only', 'Checking a Password Without Sending It', 'Keyboard Patterns to Avoid', 'Passwords on Shared Computers', 'Losing a Password: Recovery in Plain Words', 'The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index']
QUERY = 'password generator service field guide index'
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
MARKS = "!#$%&*+-=?@^_~"
def seeded_password(seed, length, sets):
    pool = "".join(sets)
    out = []
    for i in range(length):
        digest = hashlib.sha256(("%s|%d|%d" % (seed, i, len(pool))).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        out.append(pool[int(digest, 16) % len(pool)])
    return "".join(out)
def strength_bits(length, pool_size):
    return length * math.log2(pool_size)
def meter(password, pool_size):
    bits = strength_bits(len(password), pool_size)
    if bits < 40:
        return "weak"
    if bits < 60:
        return "fair"
    if bits < 90:
        return "strong"
    return "very strong"
print("Password Generator Service demo - record 24: The Password Generator Service Field Guide Index")
sets = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, MARKS]
pool = "".join(sets)
pw16 = seeded_password("record-24", 16, sets)
pw12 = seeded_password("record-24", 12, sets)
again = seeded_password("record-24", 16, sets)
other = seeded_password("record-24-other", 16, sets)
print("Seeded 16-letter password: " + pw16)
print("Seeded 12-letter password: " + pw12)
print("Pool size: %d; 16-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (len(pool), strength_bits(16, len(pool)), meter(pw16, len(pool))))
print("12-letter strength: %.1f bits (%s)" % (strength_bits(12, len(pool)), meter(pw12, len(pool))))
print("Words checked: %d" % len(QUERY.split()))
h = hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("SHA-256: " + h)
print("Deterministic: " + ("MATCH" if again == pw16 else "MISMATCH"))
print("Test: 16-letter password has 16 letters - " + ("pass" if len(pw16) == 16 else "fail"))
print("Test: same seed gives the same password - " + ("pass" if again == pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: different seed gives a different password - " + ("pass" if other != pw16 else "fail"))
print("Test: 16 letters from all four sets rates strong or better - " + ("pass" if meter(pw16, len(pool)) in ("strong", "very strong") else "fail"))
print("Test: 16-letter strength beats 12-letter strength - " + ("pass" if strength_bits(16, len(pool)) > strength_bits(12, len(pool)) else "fail"))
print("Test: generation is deterministic - " + ("pass" if hashlib.sha256((pw16 + "|" + pw12).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == h else "fail"))
